notes.title: Tongues of fire and other languages
notes.intro: At Pentecost the disciples are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak in other languages.

views.label: A pattern for a Spirit baptism today, with tongues
views.summary: Pentecostals see Pentecost as a model: believers can receive a baptism in the Spirit after conversion, marked by speaking in tongues.
views.source: Assemblies of God, Statement of Fundamental Truths, 7–8

views.label: The Spirit’s gifts continue, but tongues is not required
views.summary: Charismatics welcome tongues today without making it the necessary sign.

views.label: A unique event launching the church
views.summary: Many other Christians see Pentecost as a one-time event when the Spirit was poured out on the church, celebrated each year, with every believer receiving the Spirit at conversion or baptism.
views.source: Catechism of the Catholic Church 731–732; Westminster Confession 1.1

notes.title: “Repent and be baptized… for the forgiveness of your sins”
notes.intro: Peter’s answer to the crowd links repentance, baptism, forgiveness and the gift of the Spirit.

views.label: Baptism truly conveys forgiveness
views.summary: Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran Christians read this as baptism actually giving forgiveness and the Spirit.

views.label: Baptism is when forgiveness is received by the believer
views.summary: Churches of Christ see baptism of believers as the point at which sins are forgiven.
views.source: Everett Ferguson, The Church of Christ (1996)

views.label: Baptism follows and signifies forgiveness received by faith
views.summary: Baptists and many evangelicals read “for” as “because of” or “with a view to,” holding that forgiveness comes through faith and baptism publicly signifies it.
views.source: Baptist Faith and Message (2000), Article VII

notes.common: The promise is “for you and your children,” which some also cite for infant baptism.
